mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in the monthly CPIAUCSL inflation index above 0.3% triggers a preemptive S&P 500 forward return discount as investors anticipate rate hikes, leading to negative 20-day returns.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL crosses above 0.3% in the current month
failure_condition: Over a 12-month window, 20-day forward returns do not deviate significantly from the mean when CPIAUCSL > 0.3%, or the S&P 500 outperforms a risk-free rate proxy by more than 1%.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly rise in PAYEMS labor cost index exceeding 0.5% signals wage pressure, which precedes a negative 60-day S&P 500 forward return as profit expectations cool.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increases by more than 0.5% month-over-month
failure_condition: In regimes where PAYEMS > 0.5% monthly for 3 consecutive months, 60-day forward returns remain non-negative, or UNRATE increases in parallel by less than 0.1%.

mechanism_narrative: A consecutive monthly decline in GDPC1 personal consumption exceeding 2% suggests weakening demand, which predicts a positive 5-day S&P 500 forward return as short-term investors seek higher-yielding assets.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 declines by at least 2% over two consecutive months
failure_condition: Over 20-day windows following such declines, 5-day forward returns are not statistically different from the prior 5-day average (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A monthly drop in INDPRO manufacturing index below 95 triggers a positive 20-day S&P 500 forward return as market anticipates easing supply constraints and potential production rebound.
failure_condition: No significant positive return in the next 20 days when INDPRO remains below 95 for at least 3 months, or manufacturing momentum does not recover as expected.

mechanism_narrative: When FEDFUNDS rises above 5%, the 60-day S&P 500 forward return turns negative as investors anticipate tighter credit conditions and reduced risk appetite.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS crosses above 5% in the current month
failure_condition: Over 12 such episodes, the 60-day forward returns are not statistically negative (p > 0.05), or FEDFUNDS does not coincide with S&P 500 outperformance in subsequent months.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly increase in UNRATE above 3.5% for two consecutive months is accompanied by a positive 20-day S&P 500 forward return as higher labor costs prompt wage–price adjustments that benefit equities.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE increases by more than 0.5% month-over-month for 2 months
failure_condition: In such regimes, 20-day forward returns remain negative or flat, or other demand proxies (e.g., GDPC1) show no acceleration.

mechanism_narrative: Concurrent declines in both HOUST (housing starts) and RSAFS (retail sales) by at least 4% and 6% respectively indicate dual softening in demand sectors, producing a positive 20-day S&P 500 forward return as risk premia compress.
candidate_trigger: HOUST < prev and RSAFS < prev by at least 4% and 6% respectively in the same month
failure_condition: If either proxy recovers in the next 30 days without a corresponding S&P 500 outperformance, or the interaction effect is not captured by a multivariate Granger causality test (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: During a post-crisis recovery regime (defined by UNRATE < 3% and FEDFUNDS < 4%), a positive 60-day S&P 500 forward return is expected as policy normalization supports economic expansion.
candidate_trigger: Regime condition: UNRATE < 3% AND FEDFUNDS < 4% for 3 consecutive months
failure_condition: In this regime, 60-day forward returns are not positive in 70% of instances, or other expansion indicators (e.g., INDPRO, GDPC1) show no acceleration.
